decision: Treat "the configuration" that reconcile compares the files against as the projection (what the recorded events describe), not a copy of the files kept somewhere else
options: a byte snapshot of the files kept in .troupe/
reason: This is why reconciling after a set finds nothing to record. A byte snapshot would duplicate state the projection already holds and would not give leaf-level events.

decision: The <dir> in the watching line is the --theatre value as given, else TROUPE_THEATRE as given, else the absolute path of the current directory (never a bare '.')
reason: The line then matches what the user typed and is never a bare '.'

decision: watch prints nothing to stdout except the one watching line; events are visible only through history, and load problems go to stderr
reason: The contract asks for one stdout line

decision: If a file breaks while watch runs, watch reports it, records nothing and keeps running. If the configuration cannot load at startup, watch exits 4 without printing the line
options: exit on the first broken file
reason: Editors save partial or temporarily invalid files, so exiting would make watch unusable. At startup there is nothing to keep yet.

decision: Several quick edits may be reconciled together and recorded as their net difference
reason: The contract asks for reconciliation, not one event per save

decision: Reconcile events stand even if the command then fails with exit 3 or 5
reason: The reconcile reflects the files and is true whatever the command does next. This matches step 1 D-2 for import.

decision: Concurrency scope: watch alongside one other command is in scope. Two sets at once, a hand edit and a set on the same file at the same moment, more than one watch, and switching between troupe.yml and troupe.yaml while watching are out of contract
reason: Consistent with step 1's 'concurrent writers' exclusion
recorded_at: spec.md D-16 and Out of contract (diff.patch:821-832)

decision: watch only reads configuration files and writes none
reason: It may change nothing outside the tool's own state (step 1 FR-003)

decision: No source field is added to history to tell hand edits apart from set commands
reason: The contract does not ask for a source, so none is invented (Principle V)

decision: Supersede step 1 D-1 (hand edits not recorded) and mark it as superseded in the step 1 spec; all other step 1 rules stay in force
reason: Step 2 now records hand edits by reconciling
recorded_at: spec.md (diff.patch:591-594); spec/001 spec.md diff.patch:44-45; questions.md Q1

decision: Resolve the open points conservatively without asking the product owner
reason: None of them needed a product-owner question

decision: Reword FR-114: reconcile removes come in the order leaves were first recorded (projection order), not 'document order'
options: document order of the recorded configuration
reason: Document order stops being well defined once set has added new values, and diff_events emits removes in the order of the projection

decision: Implement reconcile as diff_events(store.leaves(), leaves(loaded.root)), reusing step 1's diff_events and recording the result in one save
reason: Keeps one definition of 'differs' (type-exact scalars_equal) and one event order (Principle IV). Formatting and comment edits then record nothing by construction.

decision: Add a reconcile flag to open_theatre: show, set and watch pass True, history passes False. On first use the theatre is imported, not reconciled.
reason: One function decides what every command does before its own work. history's exception is visible at its one call site.

decision: Use one exclusive fcntl.flock on .troupe/events.sqlite3.lock, held from just before load until events are recorded. watch holds it only around each reconcile, never while idle.
options: SQLite BEGIN EXCLUSIVE on a second connection
ignore self-written changes by remembering the bytes a set wrote
reason: Whoever comes second sees a projection that already matches. BEGIN EXCLUSIVE would self-deadlock, remembering bytes is fragile and leaves a race, and optimistic concurrency would turn the race into a failed command.

decision: Name the lock file STORE_FILENAME + '.lock'
reason: Groups it with the store's own files, and the test snapshot helper already excludes it

decision: Open the lock file O_RDWR|O_CREAT and fall back to O_RDONLY on PermissionError. Any other OSError raises a LoadError naming the lock file (exit 4).
reason: flock works on a read-only descriptor, and this is consistent with step 1's store errors
recorded_at: research.md S-3 (diff.patch:461-463); questions.md Discovery Q2 mentions the read-only check

decision: When .troupe/ does not exist, report the missing configuration file instead of the lock file
reason: Keeps the pre-step-2 error, so existing load-error tests still pass

decision: Detect changes by polling every 0.2 s and comparing the exact bytes last parsed. No mtime and no watchdog.
reason: No new dependency. The watching line becomes a true promise, save-by-rename and same-size edits are caught, and FSEvents coalescing is avoided.

decision: The snapshot holds every file in Loaded.files plus both CONFIG_NAMES candidates under .troupe/, and is rebuilt after each reconcile
reason: Creating or deleting either config name is seen, and added or removed includes are followed

decision: Build the snapshot from the parsed text re-encoded as UTF-8 rather than re-reading the files after the reconcile
options: re-read the files after the reconcile
reason: An edit made between parse and announce is still detected

decision: In the broken state, retry the reconcile on every poll and report each distinct error message only once
options: guess which paths to watch while broken
reason: While broken, the files that matter are unknown. Retrying is simpler and certain, and suppressing repeats keeps stderr readable.

decision: Handle event-store errors during a later reconcile the same way as load errors
reason: Same error path

decision: SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers only set a threading.Event, installed first thing. The loop waits with stop.wait.
reason: A reconcile in progress is never interrupted, there is no KeyboardInterrupt traceback, and exit is 0

decision: commands.watch takes an announce callback that writes to sys.stdout.buffer and flushes; watch returns ""
reason: watch must write mid-run, while the CLI keeps the output formatting

decision: No change to apply_set: set reconciles first under the lock, so its before-leaves equal the projection
reason: The recorded events are then exactly the set's own

decision: Testing approach: e2e tests with watch as a real Popen subprocess stopped by real signals, exactly-once shown by comparing histories with and without watch, and a lock-held test
reason: Principle II: break it deliberately

decision: Keep the step 1 layout and add small lock.py, sync.py and watch.py modules under config/
